1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/run-test.sh <test-file.gd | --flag-test> <fps|realtime> [timeout-seconds]
3	# The course's Assignment 7 wrapper, merged with this repository's by Claude Code (21 Nov 2026).
4	# As the course's:
5	# - <fps> runs with --fixed-fps <fps>; `realtime` runs without it, for tests that wait on audio;
6	# - the third argument is the timeout in seconds, 120 by default;
7	# - the log is logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log, or logs/<name>_realtime.log;
8	# - the exit status is 1 if the log has SHADER ERROR, SCRIPT ERROR or Failed loading resource
9	#   (a scene, clip or sheet that won't load), and 124 if the test hung.
10	# Where this repository's differs:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/run-test.sh <test-file.gd | --flag-test> <fps|realtime> [timeout-seconds]
# The course's Assignment 7 wrapper, merged with this repository's by Claude Code (21 Nov 2026).
# As the course's:
# - <fps> runs with --fixed-fps <fps>; `realtime` runs without it, for tests that wait on audio;
# - the third argument is the timeout in seconds, 120 by default;
# - the log is logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log, or logs/<name>_realtime.log;
# - the exit status is 1 if the log has SHADER ERROR, SCRIPT ERROR or Failed loading resource
#   (a scene, clip or sheet that won't load), and 124 if the test hung.
# Where this repository's differs:
# - the Godot project is the repository root, so --path . (the course's has --path godot);
# - Godot is found from GODOT, then `godot` on the PATH, then the two places the .bat launchers look;
# - an argument that starts with -- runs main.tscn with that flag (`-- --camp-test`) instead of a
#   tests/ script.
set -o pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
godot="${GODOT:-$(command -v godot || true)}"
for g in ../Godot/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe "$LOCALAPPDATA/Programs/Godot/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe"; do
	if [ -z "$godot" ] && [ -f "$g" ]; then godot="$g"; fi
done
if [ -z "$godot" ]; then echo "Godot not found: set GODOT to its executable"; exit 1; fi
mkdir -p logs
if [ "$2" = "realtime" ]; then
	fps_args=(); tag="realtime"
else
	fps_args=(--fixed-fps "$2"); tag="${2}fps"
fi
if [[ "$1" == --* ]]; then
	log="logs/${1#--}_${tag}.log"
	timeout "${3:-120}" "$godot" --headless --path . "${fps_args[@]}" -- "$1" 2>&1 | tee "$log"
else
	log="logs/$(basename "$1" .gd)_${tag}.log"
	timeout "${3:-120}" "$godot" --headless --path . --script "res://tests/$1" "${fps_args[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$log"
fi
status=$?
if grep -qE "SHADER ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR|Failed loading resource" "$log"; then status=1; fi
exit $status

content.content:
1	# The Noise Next Door
2	
3	A raccoon just wants a quiet night in his tree. Then a party starts right underneath it.
4	
5	He sneaks down to prank the partiers, gets chased into town wearing a camper's red beanie, becomes the neighbourhood's masked bandit, and is finally driven home by that same camper, just in time for the next party. It's slapstick with no dialogue: the story is told through what the player does and how people react.
6	
7	Made for CSYE 7270 (Fall 2026): one game, built up one assignment at a time.
8	
9	| Assignment | What it added | Submitted as |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| [Assignment 6: Creating Particle Effects with Godot and Claude](#assignment-6-particle-effects-in-progress) | In progress: two particle effects, the leaves bursting out of the bush and the campfire's smoke, and the campfire's life that drives the smoke | branch `assignment-6`, to be tagged `a6` |
12	| [Assignment 5: Shaders, Materials, and the Godot Shading Language](#assignment-5-shaders-and-materials) | Hand-written shaders and materials, for the campers' vision cones and a textured 3D object | tag `a5` |
13	| [Assignment 3: Your First 3D Game Assets with Claude, the Blender MCP, and Blender](#assignment-3-the-three-blender-assets) | Three props built in Blender through the Blender MCP, a Godot asset room and a headless check | tag `a3` |
14	| [Assignment 2: Generate Art, Sound, and Music for Your Game](#assignment-2-the-asset-slice) | The asset slice: the forest clearing with the generated poses, sounds and music | tag `a2` |
15	
16	After Assignment 3, the game also got its title screen, the night, the humans, level 1's camp, THE PLAN and the party's sound waves. [Run it](#run-it) covers them.
17	
18	![The storyboard](design/storyboard/storyboard-sheet.svg)
19	
20	## Run it
21	
22	You need Godot 4.7.2. The project uses the Forward+ renderer.
23	
24	- **Windows:** double-click `Play The Noise Next Door.bat`, or `Edit in Godot.bat` to open the editor. They look for Godot in the `GODOT` environment variable, then in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Godot`, then in your Downloads folder. The first run takes a few seconds longer while Godot imports the raccoon model.
25	- **Anywhere:** run `godot --path .` from this folder. On a fresh clone, first run `godot --headless --path . --import` once (or open the project in the editor), so the raccoon model is imported.
26	
27	**The title screen:** Up and Down (or W and S, or the mouse) pick a line, and Enter, Space, E or a click chooses it. Continue stays faint until there are save states to continue from. Settings has the music and effects volumes (Left and Right) and full screen, and Esc goes back. The title is the game's own world at night, seen from where your title picture was taken, so New Game changes nothing but the camera: it glides in to the close-up of the raccoon asleep in his hollow, the lullaby playing on, and W, A, S or D wakes him to start. Any `--` argument other than the title's own skips the title, so the checks below still work as before.
28	
29	**Level 1's campsite** (23 Oct 2026, `scripts/campsite.gd`): the party is set up about 20 seconds' walk east of his tree, at the end of a trodden trail along the edge of the trees: a fire pit, two tents, logs, the cooler, a table with the laptop, pizza and a donut, a speaker and string lights. The camper is pegging out his tent with a mallet, and the low-poly man and the simple girl dance by the fire on the music's beat. The speaker plays a party beat; since 25 Oct 2026 you don't hear it, you see it, as its sound waves (below). The people react to him: seen (sneak to get closer), all three take fright; the girl hides behind the low-poly man and cowers, the men stand guard, and if he hangs about they chase him off, shooing him away when they catch him. Pictures are in [design/level1/campsite/](design/level1/campsite/).
30	
31	**The bigger camp** (7 Nov 2026): the camp's clearing is now 11 m round instead of 7.5, with the trees along the trail a metre further back. The fire's circle is as it was, and everything else stands further apart: the party's corner (table, speaker, string lights and the dancers) to the north, the tents to the east and south-east, and the cooler by the table. A fourth person, the fire keeper, a second low-poly man in a mustard shirt, eats behind the table and then stokes the fire, and while he's at it he faces the camper's backpack. He's a guy, so he chases too.
32	
33	**Level 1's tasks** (24 Oct 2026, `scripts/camp_puzzles.gd`): the to-do list is now the camp's three tasks; the bin, lid, cans and gnome by his tree are still there to play with, and he still naps in his hollow, but they aren't tasks any more. The people keep to looping routines, which tell you when each one is busy: the camper pegs out his tent, then sits roasting marshmallows by the fire with his back to his backpack, then goes to the table for pizza; the low-poly man dances, then fetches a drink from the cooler; the girl dances, then warms her hands at the fire. Next to something he can use, a chalk E shows; hold E for slow jobs, and a ring fills as he works. Jobs make noise, and the people hear it and come to look ("?" over their heads), but the music drowns a lot of it out, and while they dance they're lost in the music and see less. The tasks:
34	- **Steal the marshmallows:** while the camper roasts with his back to it, hold E at his backpack to unzip it; the bag tumbles out. Carry it home to his stash under his tree. Running with it, it crinkles.
35	- **Turn the music off:** hold E at the plug under the table to tug it out with his teeth. The music stops, which ticks it off, and the dancers stop dead for two seconds: get away then. Then everyone wonders where the music went, and the low-poly man finds the plug wherever he left it and plugs it back in. Without the music, every noise carries further.
36	- **Raid the cooler:** hold E to nose its lid open (a clunk; since the cooler moved by the table on 7 Nov 2026, the camper by the fire is too far off to hear it, but with the music off the low-poly man hears it where he dances), or wait for the low-poly man, who sometimes leaves it open after his drink. Take the sausages home.
37	- **Caught carrying their things,** a man snatches them back and the puzzle resets: the bag zipped back in, the sausages back in the shut cooler.
38	
39	There's no ending yet. Pictures are in [design/level1/tasks/](design/level1/tasks/).
40	
41	**The tutorial at the camp and the campers' cones** (26 Oct 2026, `scripts/camp_tutorial.gd`, `scripts/camp_person.gd`, `scripts/vision_cone.gd`): on the way there, the only task is to investigate the music. When he reaches the camp, the game pauses and a note at the bottom says to press Tab. THE PLAN opens with the camp's three tasks on it, under one main task, Rock the party, and the note says to sneak past them; Tab again, and the game carries on. Only then can the campers see him, and their cones show on the ground: pale yellow while they watch, shorter while he sneaks. The moment one spots him, that one's cone turns red for 2 seconds, and then all the cones go while they guard, chase and shoo as before. Once he's got away, they look about, confused, with "??" over their heads, then walk back; each one's cone comes back 5 seconds after they start back. The fades on the cones are still to come, with the cone shader for Assignment 5.
42	
43	**The tutorial, remade** (7 Nov 2026, `scripts/camp_tutorial.gd`, `scripts/spotlight.gd`): THE PLAN is now called **TO DO**, and the tutorial plays as a short scene with as few words as possible.
44	- **The pan:** once he can see the party (its speaker on the screen, or him well into the clearing), the game slows right down behind a dark layer and the camera pans over the campers, the marshmallows and the cooler, a word or two on each.

# The Noise Next Door

A raccoon just wants a quiet night in his tree. Then a party starts right underneath it.

He sneaks down to prank the partiers, gets chased into town wearing a camper's red beanie, becomes the neighbourhood's masked bandit, and is finally driven home by that same camper, just in time for the next party. It's slapstick with no dialogue: the story is told through what the player does and how people react.

Made for CSYE 7270 (Fall 2026): one game, built up one assignment at a time.

| Assignment | What it added | Submitted as |
|---|---|---|
| [Assignment 6: Creating Particle Effects with Godot and Claude](#assignment-6-particle-effects-in-progress) | In progress: two particle effects, the leaves bursting out of the bush and the campfire's smoke, and the campfire's life that drives the smoke | branch `assignment-6`, to be tagged `a6` |
| [Assignment 5: Shaders, Materials, and the Godot Shading Language](#assignment-5-shaders-and-materials) | Hand-written shaders and materials, for the campers' vision cones and a textured 3D object | tag `a5` |
| [Assignment 3: Your First 3D Game Assets with Claude, the Blender MCP, and Blender](#assignment-3-the-three-blender-assets) | Three props built in Blender through the Blender MCP, a Godot asset room and a headless check | tag `a3` |
| [Assignment 2: Generate Art, Sound, and Music for Your Game](#assignment-2-the-asset-slice) | The asset slice: the forest clearing with the generated poses, sounds and music | tag `a2` |

After Assignment 3, the game also got its title screen, the night, the humans, level 1's camp, THE PLAN and the party's sound waves. [Run it](#run-it) covers them.

![The storyboard](design/storyboard/storyboard-sheet.svg)

## Run it

You need Godot 4.7.2. The project uses the Forward+ renderer.

- **Windows:** double-click `Play The Noise Next Door.bat`, or `Edit in Godot.bat` to open the editor. They look for Godot in the `GODOT` environment variable, then in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Godot`, then in your Downloads folder. The first run takes a few seconds longer while Godot imports the raccoon model.
- **Anywhere:** run `godot --path .` from this folder. On a fresh clone, first run `godot --headless --path . --import` once (or open the project in the editor), so the raccoon model is imported.

**The title screen:** Up and Down (or W and S, or the mouse) pick a line, and Enter, Space, E or a click chooses it. Continue stays faint until there are save states to continue from. Settings has the music and effects volumes (Left and Right) and full screen, and Esc goes back. The title is the game's own world at night, seen from where your title picture was taken, so New Game changes nothing but the camera: it glides in to the close-up of the raccoon asleep in his hollow, the lullaby playing on, and W, A, S or D wakes him to start. Any `--` argument other than the title's own skips the title, so the checks below still work as before.

**Level 1's campsite** (23 Oct 2026, `scripts/campsite.gd`): the party is set up about 20 seconds' walk east of his tree, at the end of a trodden trail along the edge of the trees: a fire pit, two tents, logs, the cooler, a table with the laptop, pizza and a donut, a speaker and string lights. The camper is pegging out his tent with a mallet, and the low-poly man and the simple girl dance by the fire on the music's beat. The speaker plays a party beat; since 25 Oct 2026 you don't hear it, you see it, as its sound waves (below). The people react to him: seen (sneak to get closer), all three take fright; the girl hides behind the low-poly man and cowers, the men stand guard, and if he hangs about they chase him off, shooing him away when they catch him. Pictures are in [design/level1/campsite/](design/level1/campsite/).

**The bigger camp** (7 Nov 2026): the camp's clearing is now 11 m round instead of 7.5, with the trees along the trail a metre further back. The fire's circle is as it was, and everything else stands further apart: the party's corner (table, speaker, string lights and the dancers) to the north, the tents to the east and south-east, and the cooler by the table. A fourth person, the fire keeper, a second low-poly man in a mustard shirt, eats behind the table and then stokes the fire, and while he's at it he faces the camper's backpack. He's a guy, so he chases too.

**Level 1's tasks** (24 Oct 2026, `scripts/camp_puzzles.gd`): the to-do list is now the camp's three tasks; the bin, lid, cans and gnome by his tree are still there to play with, and he still naps in his hollow, but they aren't tasks any more. The people keep to looping routines, which tell you when each one is busy: the camper pegs out his tent, then sits roasting marshmallows by the fire with his back to his backpack, then goes to the table for pizza; the low-poly man dances, then fetches a drink from the cooler; the girl dances, then warms her hands at the fire. Next to something he can use, a chalk E shows; hold E for slow jobs, and a ring fills as he works. Jobs make noise, and the people hear it and come to look ("?" over their heads), but the music drowns a lot of it out, and while they dance they're lost in the music and see less. The tasks:
- **Steal the marshmallows:** while the camper roasts with his back to it, hold E at his backpack to unzip it; the bag tumbles out. Carry it home to his stash under his tree. Running with it, it crinkles.
- **Turn the music off:** hold E at the plug under the table to tug it out with his teeth. The music stops, which ticks it off, and the dancers stop dead for two seconds: get away then. Then everyone wonders where the music went, and the low-poly man finds the plug wherever he left it and plugs it back in. Without the music, every noise carries further.
- **Raid the cooler:** hold E to nose its lid open (a clunk; since the cooler moved by the table on 7 Nov 2026, the camper by the fire is too far off to hear it, but with the music off the low-poly man hears it where he dances), or wait for the low-poly man, who sometimes leaves it open after his drink. Take the sausages home.
- **Caught carrying their things,** a man snatches them back and the puzzle resets: the bag zipped back in, the sausages back in the shut cooler.

There's no ending yet. Pictures are in [design/level1/tasks/](design/level1/tasks/).

**The tutorial at the camp and the campers' cones** (26 Oct 2026, `scripts/camp_tutorial.gd`, `scripts/camp_person.gd`, `scripts/vision_cone.gd`): on the way there, the only task is to investigate the music. When he reaches the camp, the game pauses and a note at the bottom says to press Tab. THE PLAN opens with the camp's three tasks on it, under one main task, Rock the party, and the note says to sneak past them; Tab again, and the game carries on. Only then can the campers see him, and their cones show on the ground: pale yellow while they watch, shorter while he sneaks. The moment one spots him, that one's cone turns red for 2 seconds, and then all the cones go while they guard, chase and shoo as before. Once he's got away, they look about, confused, with "??" over their heads, then walk back; each one's cone comes back 5 seconds after they start back. The fades on the cones are still to come, with the cone shader for Assignment 5.

**The tutorial, remade** (7 Nov 2026, `scripts/camp_tutorial.gd`, `scripts/spotlight.gd`): THE PLAN is now called **TO DO**, and the tutorial plays as a short scene with as few words as possible.
- **The pan:** once he can see the party (its speaker on the screen, or him well into the clearing), the game slows right down behind a dark layer and the camera pans over the campers, the marshmallows and the cooler, a word or two on each.
- **The laugh:** back on him, he chitters on his own, the cones come on, and the nearest camper hears it and comes to look.
- **Hide:** the campers freeze where they are and the bush at the camp's west side is lit ("Hide!"), and it waits until he's in it. Walk into it and he dives in with a hop: the bush rustles, he's gone, and his eyes peek out of it, blinking. In it, nobody can see him or catch him. Nobody comes for him either: whoever saw him or took fright stands where they are, confused ("??"), and looks about, and the camera shows the one who saw him ("He lost you"); then they all go back to work. A move key hops him out that way; hold Ctrl and he comes out sneaking.
- **Roasted marshmallows** (remade later on 7 Nov 2026): once they're all back at work, the camper roasts one at the fire, turns round to set it on a plate on the log behind him, and goes back for more. The first one on the plate stops the camp as the hide did: the campers freeze, the plate is lit under the dark layer, and the raccoon thinks of food. There are no words. Take it with E, and they come to: the camper, turned to the plate, spots him, the others take fright, and the men chase him. Caught, he's shooed but keeps it, and E doesn't drop it. Once they've lost him and are all back at work, the E shows over him (not while he's in the bush): hold it, and he sits up straight, ears up, holding it in both front paws and looking down at it. He eats it in three bites: each time he lifts it to his mouth as his head dips to meet it, chomps, and chews with quick little nods, eyes squeezed shut and head tilting, while his paws lower it again, smaller each time ("Yum!"). Let go, and he stands with what's left in his mouth. The eating is laid over his bored animation's sit in code (`scripts/raccoon_eat.gd`, with Godot's two-bone IK for his paws), since there's no Blender here to add an animation to his rig.
- **The list:** then Tab brings up the TO DO list to read (hover over a task to see how it's done); Tab again, and the camp plays as before.

**The party next door** (25 Oct 2026, `scripts/sound_waves.gd`): under the title the night is quiet; New Game starts the party up. You don't hear it (his lullaby plays on); you see it, as its sound waves. They are drawn like the thought icons, three hand-scribbled wavy white lines. On the beat, while the speaker's off the screen, a set pulses on the edge of the screen the music's coming from, so you can always tell which way to go; once the speaker's on the screen, the sets come out of the speaker itself. Asleep in his hollow, he sleeps on through it, untroubled. Pictures are in [design/level1/waves/](design/level1/waves/).

**Controls:** WASD or the arrow keys to move, Shift to run, Ctrl or C to sneak, F to jump (tap it for a small hop, hold it for a full jump), E or a click to grab or drop, Space to chitter, and the mouse wheel to zoom. Walk into a tree to climb it. Then W and S climb up and down, A and D go round the trunk, and E or F lets go. Climb to the top of the home pine to get into the hollow. Esc pauses. M turns the music on and off (since 7 Nov 2026 it starts off), and N does the same for the sound effects. Tab brings up the TO DO list (THE PLAN until 7 Nov 2026), the level's tasks on a torn notebook page, crossed off as they're done (the camp's tasks appear on it with the tutorial at the camp); the task to follow now waits at the bottom of the screen, and a task just done comes up there crossed off. V opens a panel for trying out camera views live; its "Copy numbers" button copies the settings.

**Developer keys** (debug runs only, which include runs from the editor; added 8 Nov 2026): **F1** opens the developer menu (`scripts/dev_menu.gd`). It restarts the level at a point: from the den, arriving at the camp, the tutorial's roasting, or free play with the campfire out or burning. It shows the fire's strength and what the fire keeper is doing, and it can put the fire out or set it burning. The same points start a run from the command line with `-- --dev-start=<den|camp|roast|free|fire>`. **F9** turns vsync off and on, for Assignment 6's frame-rate comparison; the window's title says which. Neither key is used by the game.

**The automated sound check:** run `godot --headless --path . -- --sound-test`. It plays a scripted input sequence, counts how often each sound effect starts, and checks the music's pause, mute, loop and end behaviour. It prints a table, and its exit code is 0 only if every check passes (`scripts/sound_test.gd`).

**The campsite check:** run `godot --headless --path . --audio-driver Dummy -- --camp-test`. It puts the raccoon near the camp sneaking, in plain sight, lingering, up a tree, gone and chittering out of sight, and checks how each of the three takes it (`scripts/camp_test.gd`). Add `--camp-shots=<folder>` in a window for pictures.

**The tasks check:** run `godot --headless --path . --audio-driver Dummy -- --tasks-test`. It walks the three through their routines, then plays each task with E as you would: the marshmallows caught and snatched back, then stolen cleanly and taken home; the music off, the dancers frozen, and the plug found and put back; a noise drowned by the music but heard without it; and the cooler raided. It checks the to-do list ticks each one off (`scripts/tasks_test.gd`). Add `--tasks-shots=<folder>` in a window for pictures.

**The sound waves check:** run `godot --headless --path . --audio-driver Dummy -- --waves-test`. It checks a set of waves goes out on the party's beat and fades after its time; that by his tree and along the trail they're on the edge of the screen the music comes from, and at the camp they come out of the speaker; and that with the music stopped no more come (`scripts/waves_test.gd`). Add `--waves-shots=<folder>` in a window for pictures.

**THE PLAN check:** run `godot --headless --path . --audio-driver Dummy -- --plan-test`. It brings the plan up with Tab and puts it away, checks V has the camera panel, then ticks tasks off and checks what comes up at the bottom of the screen: a task just done, crossed off, and gone again; the key task waiting there until he reaches the camp; and the page crossing off what's been done (`scripts/plan_test.gd`). Add `--plan-shots=<folder>` in a window for pictures.

**The tutorial and cones check:** run `godot --headless --path . -- --cones-test`. It puts the raccoon in plain sight at the camp and checks that nobody sees him before the tutorial; that the tutorial pauses the game, ignores Esc, shows Rock the party and its tasks on Tab and carries on after a second Tab; that the spotter's cone is red, every cone shows through the red, and every cone goes 2.5 s after the spotting; that after the chase each of them is confused for 3 s and their cone comes back 5 s after they start back; and that Rock the party is ticked off with its last task (`scripts/cones_test.gd`). It measures the times on the game's clock, so it passes the same at `--fixed-fps 30`, `60` and `144`. Add `--cones-shots=<folder>` in a window for pictures. The other checks skip the tutorial. Since 7 Nov 2026 it goes through the remade tutorial (slowed behind the dark layer, Tab, Enter on the marshmallows), with its intro and guided steps turned off.

**The tutorial check:** run `bash scripts/run-test.sh --tutorial-test 60`. It plays the remade tutorial through, all of it on, as a player would with Tab and E: the pan, the laugh and being seen, the campers frozen till he hides, and in the bush the ones who saw him confused where they stand, nobody coming for him. Then a chase to the bush (set going by the check) that can't catch him, hopping out sneaking, the plate stopping the camp with no words, taking one with E, the campers alerted and the men chasing, eating it sitting up once they've calmed, unnoticed, and the TO DO list (`scripts/tutorial_test.gd`, 29 checks). Add `--tutorial-shots=<folder>` in a window for pictures.

**The title screen check:** run `godot --headless --path . -- --title-test`. It moves through the menu with the keys and the mouse, changes the volumes and checks they reach the buses and the settings file, checks the menu's keys leave him asleep, then chooses New Game and checks the way in: the same scene throughout with nothing laid over it, the camera ending in the nap close-up, the lullaby carrying on, the party next door quiet under the title and starting with New Game, silent, with the lullaby playing on and his nap going on untroubled by it, that first nap not counting as one of his naps, and a move key waking him and bringing in the forest music and the key task at the bottom of the screen. It puts your settings file back afterwards (`scripts/title_test.gd`). Run in a window with `--title-shots=<folder>` as well, it saves pictures of the way in. `godot --path . -- --title-shot=out.png` saves a picture of the title screen.

To redraw the storyboard after editing it, run `python design/storyboard/make_thumbnails.py`. To remake the character-sheet images and the raccoon's cut-outs, run `godot --path . --script res://design/character/make_character_sheet.gd`, then copy the five cut-outs the slice uses into `assets/characters/raccoon/`. For the stump, run `godot --headless --path . --script res://design/environment/make_props.gd`. For the sound loops, run `python design/sfx/make_sfx_loops.py`. To update the game's raccoon after editing `raccoon.blend`, run `blender -b assets/characters/raccoon.blend --python assets/characters/export_raccoon.py`.

## Assignment 6: particle effects (in progress)

*Creating Particle Effects with Godot and Claude*, on the branch `assignment-6`, to be submitted as the tag `a6`. Godot 4.7.2, Forward+.

### What this assignment added

- **Effect A, the leaf burst** ([effects/leaf_burst.tscn](effects/leaf_burst.tscn)): leaves and a puff of flecks burst out of the camp's bush when he dives in, and a burst half the size when he hops out. Its job is to tell you you're hidden, out of sight of whoever's after you, and then that you're out and can be seen again.
  - Two `GPUParticles3D`, **Leaves** and **Puff**, under one `Node3D`, each with a `ParticleProcessMaterial` and a `StandardMaterial3D`.
  - **Its event:** the bush's `dived()` ends by emitting `hiding_changed(inside)` ([scripts/hide_spot.gd](scripts/hide_spot.gd)). [scripts/leaf_bursts.gd](scripts/leaf_bursts.gd) listens, puts a fresh copy at the bush each time and frees it on a timer.
  - **Its retrigger rule is overlap:** diving in and hopping straight out gives two bursts alive at once.
- **Effect B, the campfire smoke** ([effects/campfire_smoke.tscn](effects/campfire_smoke.tscn)): a soft grey column over the fire pit while the fire burns, thicker the stronger it burns. It warns you the fire is up, so near the camp you should crouch.
  - One `GPUParticles3D`, **Smoke**.
  - **A feedback loop:** every frame, [scripts/campfire_smoke.gd](scripts/campfire_smoke.gd) sets its `amount_ratio` to the fire's `strength`, and `emitting` to whether the fire is burning. `amount` never changes.
  - **What Effect A doesn't use:** the value-driven `amount_ratio`, turbulence, a scale curve (the puffs grow as they rise), a box emission shape, `preprocess` (a burning fire has its column on the first frame) and a soft round texture.
- **The campfire's life, which drives the smoke** ([scripts/camp_fire.gd](scripts/camp_fire.gd)):
  - The fire is out at the start. The fire keeper builds it a log at a time from the woodpile, and it burns down by itself.
  - E at the bucket douses it.
  - While it burns, he's spotted walking or running upright near it, and standing in its light he's seen half as far again. Crouch.
  - The other game work this assignment brought (the tent, the tutorial's pan and its "You've been caught!", dropping what he's caught with) is in [TEST-REPORT.md](https://github.com/Abhinow1997/the-noise-next-door/blob/a6/TEST-REPORT.md#assignment-6-particle-effects-and-the-bigger-camp).
- **The previews and their frame strips** (fixture captures, Movie Maker at 30 fps, 1280 × 720):
  - [previews/leaf_burst_preview.tscn](previews/leaf_burst_preview.tscn), with its strips in `captures/leaf_burst/`;
  - [previews/campfire_smoke_preview.tscn](previews/campfire_smoke_preview.tscn), with its strips in `captures/campfire_smoke/`.
- **Tuning:** one revision for each effect, both kept ([TUNING.md](https://github.com/Abhinow1997/the-noise-next-door/blob/a6/TUNING.md)):
  - the leaves' gravity went from −3.5 to −6.0, so they flutter down after the burst;
  - the smoke's peak alpha went from 0.45 to 0.25, so it reads as haze, not a glowing cloud.
- **The checks:**
  - **Configuration:** [tests/test_leaf_burst_config.gd](tests/test_leaf_burst_config.gd) and [tests/test_campfire_smoke_config.gd](tests/test_campfire_smoke_config.gd) read every setting in the brief back from the scene files. Two mutations of Effect A's scene, a Godot 3 property name and a changed `amount`, each make it exit 1.
  - **State:** `--leaf-burst-test` ([tests/leaf_burst_state_test.gd](tests/leaf_burst_state_test.gd)) runs the game through real input. `--smoke-test` and `--smoke-load-test` ([tests/campfire_smoke_state_test.gd](tests/campfire_smoke_state_test.gd)) do the same, with the fire cold and burning at load.
  - **Price:** [tests/cost_effects.gd](tests/cost_effects.gd), the headless CPU price against an empty-scene control.
- **The price:**
  - **Headless CPU:** 0.005 ms a frame for the empty scene, 1.016 for the game with both effects off, 1.018 with Effect A at its peak and 1.008 with Effect B at its heaviest. The two effects can't be told apart from "off", as predicted: a headless run draws nothing and runs no GPU particle process.
  - **GPU, on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU at 1280 × 720:** Effect A added +0.05 ms (budget 0.2 ms) and Effect B +0.03 ms (budget 0.3 ms), both within the noise. These were read with [tools/gpu_time_effects.gd](tools/gpu_time_effects.gd), a windowed script that reads the GPU timer the Visual Profiler shows. In the Visual Profiler itself, one frame I read shows 2.96 ms of GPU time in all, with 0.01 ms for "Update GPUParticles", the particles' process step ([TEST-REPORT.md](TEST-REPORT.md#the-gpu-price-8-nov-2026)).
- **The shader Godot generates for a `ParticleProcessMaterial`:** [shaders/particles_generated.gdshader](shaders/particles_generated.gdshader), converted in the editor from a copy of the smoke's process material. Nothing in the game uses it.

## Assignment 5: shaders and materials

*Shaders, Materials, and the Godot Shading Language*, on the branch `assignment-5`, submitted as the tag `a5`.

### What this assignment added

- **The campers' vision cones, coloured by my shader** ([shaders/vision_cone.gdshader](shaders/vision_cone.gdshader)):
  - pale yellow while a camper watches;
  - red for 2 seconds on the cone of whoever spots him, starting over if he's spotted again;
  - then every cone fades out over 0.5 s, and each comes back, yellow, about 5 s after its camper calms down.

  Each cone has its own `ShaderMaterial` (`scripts/vision_cone.gd`). [scripts/cone_driver.gd](scripts/cone_driver.gd) sets each one's `alarm` and `shown` every frame from the camp's `spotted_at` and `spotters` (`scripts/campsite.gd`), and writes nothing else.
- **The cooler, with my textured shader** ([shaders/cooler_paint.gdshader](shaders/cooler_paint.gdshader)):
  - two materials from it, [materials/cooler_body.tres](materials/cooler_body.tres) (scuffed red metal, changed from blue on 1 Nov) and [materials/cooler_lid.tres](materials/cooler_lid.tres) (smoother white);
  - both behind the glb's per-material Use External, so every cooler gets them;
  - the textures are Poly Haven's Blue Metal Plate, by Rob Tuytel, CC0 ([credits](assets/textures/blue_metal_plate/ATTRIBUTION.md)): a colour texture read with `source_color`, and a roughness map and a GL normal map read as data.
- **The hint experiment** ([hint_experiment/hint_experiment.tscn](hint_experiment/hint_experiment.tscn)): a 3×1 PNG of greys 64, 128 and 192, sampled with and without `source_color` on one quad split in two.
- **The checks:**
  - `--cone-shader-test`, which drives the cones through real spottings at 30, 60 and 144 fps;

### For the grader: the assets in Godot, with their sizes

The asset room, `asset_room/asset_room.tscn`, shows every asset at game size on a floor under the forest level's light, beside the raccoon for scale. Each has a label with its size as Godot measures it: W × D × H in metres, where H is the height (Godot's Y is up).

**You need Godot 4.7.2 stable**, the standard build (not .NET), from the [Godot download archive](https://godotengine.org/download/archive/). You don't need Blender: Godot loads the exported `.glb` files, and the `.blend` sources are marked for Godot to skip.

**Open it:**
- **Windows:** double-click `Look at the A3 assets.bat`. It looks for Godot in this order:
  - the `GODOT` variable;
  - a `Godot` folder beside this repo (`..\Godot\`);
  - `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Godot\`;

  If yours is somewhere else, set `GODOT` to the path of its `.exe`.

  godot --headless --path . --import

**Importing:** both launchers import the models first, because a scene started from the command line doesn't import anything itself. On a fresh copy of this folder, with no `.godot` cache, the import took 8 s here; after that it takes about 4 s.

**Controls:**
- Drag to orbit and use the wheel to zoom.

## Assignment 2: the asset slice

*Generate Art, Sound, and Music for Your Game*. Submitted as the tag `a2`.

### What the slice demonstrates

The slice is the prototype's forest clearing, with its five-task to-do list, dressed with the generated assets:
- **The raccoon, drawn with his generated poses:** idle, running, sneaking, bored (after 5 s of standing still), asleep in the hollow, and climbing. He's mirrored when he faces left.
- **A generated tree stump** (ENV-STUMP), placed in the clearing, with collision.
- **Four generated sound effects, each tied to an event:** running (a loop while Shift-running), climbing (a loop while moving on a trunk), his chitter (Space) and a laugh when a task is ticked off.
- **A seamless generated music loop:** it's muffled and quieter while paused, dips under the task laugh, and fades out when every task is done. M and N mute the music and the effects.

[TEST-REPORT.md](https://github.com/Abhinow1997/the-noise-next-door/blob/a2/TEST-REPORT.md) shows each of these in the game, and [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md) logs how each asset was made.

### Known limitations (Assignment 2)

- **Static images:** each state is one picture, so his changes of state snap. The author found the animation "a bit blovcky".
- **No back views:** walking away from the camera still shows his front.
- **Climbing** reuses the sneak pose, turned upright.
- **No humans, so no failure state:** the slice doesn't cover being caught, and only 4 of the storyboard's 15 panels are partly covered.
- **The chitter and the task laugh** are two takes of the same laugh.
- **Contrast:** his grey fur is close to the grass in brightness (1.3 to 2.0:1), so his charcoal markings carry his shape.
- **Muted play** was only partly readable, and which moments were lost wasn't noted. The sound levels raised after the playtest haven't been re-checked by ear.
- **Large files, kept out of GitHub:** four of the original music tracks in `design/music/` are over 25 MB, and two laugh originals there are MP3s.
  - They were in the repo until 15 Oct 2026. They're no longer tracked, and `.gitignore` keeps them out, but Git's older commits still hold them.
  - They're in the course media storage: **link to add**.
  - The game doesn't load any of them: it plays the cut loops in `assets/audio/`. The source ZIP leaves them out.

[TEST-REPORT.md](https://github.com/Abhinow1997/the-noise-next-door/blob/a2/TEST-REPORT.md) has the details and the next steps.

## Started from

This project started from **Raccoon Mischief**, the first prototype of this game, and it keeps building on it.

The prototype is a raccoon in a fenced garden with a five-task to-do list. Everything in it is built in GDScript when the game runs: the raccoon is a procedural low-poly model, and there are no image or sound files. It doesn't play the storyboard's story yet.

Two changes were made with Claude Code on 4 Oct 2026, before this repo existed:
- The launchers find Godot on any machine.
- The raccoon can be smoothed, using `smooth_loft()` in `scripts/lowpoly.gd` and the `smooth` setting in `scripts/raccoon_model.gd`. Turning `smooth` off brings back the original faceted look.

## Who made what

- **The author:** the prototype, the story, and the design decisions. The provenance notes at the end of CONCEPT.md and STORYBOARD.md list them.
- **Claude Code:** drafts and wording for the docs, the storyboard thumbnails (drawn in code), the two prototype changes above, the raccoon model in `assets/characters/` (built in Blender with Python) and the code that puts it in the game, tree climbing, the camera code and its camera panel (the camera view itself is the author's pick), the character-sheet images and pose cut-outs (`design/character/make_character_sheet.gd`), the music and sound-effect loop cuts (`design/sfx/make_sfx_loops.py`), drawing the raccoon with the generated images (`scripts/raccoon_sprite.gd`), placing the stump, wiring up the sounds, mute and pause, the automated sound check (`scripts/sound_test.gd`), level 1's campsite (`scripts/campsite.gd`) with the people's dance and hammer animations, THE PLAN, the task list on Tab, built from the author's picture (`scripts/plan_note.gd`), and this README.
- **Generative models, run by the author:**
  - Google Gemini for every image: the raccoon's style target (made before any design doc was committed), his pose images, the other character and scene references, and the ground texture;
  - Suno for the five music tracks, and ElevenLabs for all the sound effects.

  [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md) logs every generation. Claude Code generated none of them: it cut out the poses and cut the loops.

  - "Human Basic Shapes: male and female basemesh" by **Josephbburg** ([Blend Swap 72307](http://www.blendswap.com/blends/view/72307)), under [Creative Commons Attribution 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). This credit is required.

This credit is required. The fire keeper (added 7 Nov 2026) is a second copy of it, wearing a recoloured copy of its texture (changed by Claude Code; see SOURCES.md, Assignment 6).

554		var still := false

func _change_animation(anim_name: String) -> void:
	var from := _anim.current_animation

func _rigged_state(delta: float) -> String:
	var still := false
	var state := "idle"
	# A leap holds poses from the run; asleep, he's curled up from the moment he
	# starts dozing until he gets up.
	if leap >= 0.0:
		state = "run"
	elif sleep > 0.0:
		state = "sleep"
	elif hopping:
		state = "run"
	elif climbing:
		state = "climb"
	elif crouch > 0.5:

	elif speed > RUN_FROM:

	elif speed > 0.15 or absf(yaw_rate) > TURN_STEP:

## True while he's running on his own (run_off).
func running_off() -> bool:
	return _run_off_left > 0.0


## Jumps: now if he's on the ground, or as soon as he lands (see JUMP_BUFFER).
func jump() -> void:
	_jump_press = JUMP_BUFFER


## Lands a jump once he's back down, and poses him through it. Leaving, his hind legs
## push off and he squashes for a moment; at the top he's stretched out; he tips nose
## up on the way up and nose down coming down. Landed, his front paws take it, he
## squashes as hard as he came down and his hind legs come in, and then he's back in
## his own stride. `rising` is how fast he was going up (m/s) before this tick's move.
func _jump_pose(delta: float, rising: float) -> void:
	var lift := sqrt(2.0 * JUMP_GRAVITY * JUMP_HEIGHT)
	if jumping and _air_t > 0.0 and rising <= 0.0 and is_on_floor():
		jumping = false
		_land_t = 0.0
		_land_hard = clampf(-rising / lift, 0.3, 1.0)
		_land_pitch = model.pitch
		landed.emit()
	if jumping:
		_air_t += delta
		model.leap = _keyed(JUMP_AIR, clampf((1.0 - velocity.y / lift) * 0.5, 0.0, 1.0))
		model.squash = 0.5 * maxf(0.0, 1.0 - _air_t / 0.1)
		var tip := clampf(atan2(velocity.y, maxf(_speed, 1.5)) * 0.35, -0.35, 0.3)
		model.pitch = tip * smoothstep(0.0, 0.08, _air_t)
	elif _land_t >= 0.0:
		_land_t += delta
		var f := minf(_land_t / LAND_TIME, 1.0)
		model.leap = lerpf(1.48, 1.78, f)
		model.squash = 0.8 * _land_hard * sin(PI * sqrt(f))
		model.pitch = _land_pitch * (1.0 - smoothstep(0.0, 0.6, f))
		if f >= 1.0:
			_end_jump()


## Out of a jump's poses, landed or not.
func _end_jump() -> void:
	jumping = false
	_land_t = -1.0
	model.leap = -1.0
	model.squash = 0.0
	model.pitch = 0.0

  the course's `godot/shaders/`, `godot/animations/`, `godot/tests/` are `shaders/`, `animations/`, `tests/` here.
  Renderer Forward+; 1280 × 720 (`project.godot`); `physics/common/physics_interpolation=true` (`project.godot`).
- **Scene:** `res://main.tscn` (`run/main_scene`) is one `Node3D` running `scripts/main.gd`, which builds the level and
  adds `Campsite.new()` (`scripts/campsite.gd`). There is no `animations/` folder yet.

### The jump: imported 3D rig (`CHANGE-BRIEF.md`, "The two clips")
- **Rig:** `assets/characters/raccoon_v2.glb` (from `raccoon_v2.blend` by `assets/characters/export_raccoon_v2.py`; its
  actions keyed in `design/character/raccoon_v2/anim.py`). Import: `animation/fps=24`, `_subresources={}`
  (`raccoon_v2.glb.import:34,42`). Loaded by `_build_rigged()` (`scripts/raccoon_model.gd:375`); the model's scene is
  `raccoon_model.tscn`. The `AnimationPlayer` is found in the instanced rig (`raccoon_model.gd:384`) and held in `_anim`.
- **New clips** `jump` and `jump_land` go in the `.glb` as Blender actions (keyed in `anim.py`); loop modes go in the
  `.import`'s `_subresources`, replacing the runtime loop at `raccoon_model.gd:385-386`.
- **State machine:** the state lives in `scripts/player.gd` (`jump()` :431, `_jump_pose()` :440, `_end_jump()` :465,
  `jumping` :159, `signal landed` :13, the `JUMP_*`, `AIR_CONTROL`, `LAND_TIME` constants :93-100; `_physics_process()`
  :251 sets `model.jumping`). The clips are picked in `scripts/raccoon_model.gd`: `_process_rigged()` :460 →
  `_rigged_state()` :553 → `_change_animation()` :540. No `AnimationTree`.
- **His mouth:** `mouth`, a `Marker3D` on a `BoneAttachment3D` on the `head` bone (`raccoon_model.gd:392-400`).
- **Readers of the jump:** `scripts/cone_driver.gd:96` (`jumping`); `_on_landed()` (`scripts/campsite.gd:539`, `HEAR_STEPS`
  6 m, :110); `scripts/tasks_test.gd:260-274` (a jump's landing heard).

### The balloon's float: `Sprite3D` + `AnimationPlayer` frame track
- **Sheets:** `assets/sprites/balloons/balloon_{red_4,yellow,blue_4}.png` (also green, purple), 48 × 64 px, `hframes` 3,
  `vframes` 2; float cells 0–2, pop 3–5 (`assets/sprites/balloons/ATTRIBUTION.md`; CC-BY-SA 4.0, credit line there).
- **Placement:** by the party's table and speaker, `TABLE` and `SPEAKER` (`scripts/campsite.gd:81,83`); the pop is heard
  `HEAR_CHITTER` 8 m (:105). The balloon's scene, script and clips don't exist yet; their paths are not chosen.
- **Moth (extra):** `assets/sprites/cutebugs/bugs.png` (`ATTRIBUTION.md` there, CC0), shown while `burning()`

### Tests: always `bash scripts/run-test.sh <test> <fps|realtime> [timeout-s]`, from the repo root
- `--name` runs `main.tscn` with that flag (parsed in `scripts/main.gd:399-470`); anything else runs `res://tests/<file>`
  with `--script`. Headless. `<fps>` adds `--fixed-fps <fps>`; `realtime` omits it (audio, the clock). Timeout 120 s by
  default. Log `logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log` or `_realtime.log`. Exit 1 on `SHADER ERROR`, `SCRIPT ERROR` or `Failed

## Headless facts
- A headless run uses a dummy renderer (it reports no video adapter): it draws no particles and runs no GPU
  particle process. Node state (emitting, one_shot, amount_ratio, visibility, instance counts) is observable; the
  look is not. On 4.7.2 a one-shot `GPUParticles3D` turns `emitting` off within a few frames and never emits
  `finished` (read back on 7 Nov 2026), so nothing may wait on `finished`: free a burst on a timer.
- A GPU effect's headless CPU price is near zero by construction.
- Frame strips come from a windowed Movie Maker run, which I start.
- Under `--fixed-fps`, game time follows frames, not the clock; physics runs at 60 ticks a second at every rate.
## Current change
@CHANGE-BRIEF.md

## Ownership
- Every file in `shaders/` is hand-written by the human and is never edited by an agent: not created, rewritten,
  reformatted or "fixed". If a shader looks wrong, report it and stop.
- Clips live as resources: in `animations/` (`.tres`/`.res`), in the scene that owns them (the balloon's `.tscn`), or,
  for the rig, as actions in `raccoon_v2.glb` with import settings in its `.import`. Never built in code at runtime: no
  `Animation.new()`, `add_track()`, `track_insert_key()` or `loop_mode =` in game scripts.
- Assignment 6's effect settings stay in `effects/` scenes; scripts only instance, place, set `amount_ratio`, and free.
- The brief's tables are the source of every timing; a change starts as a dated revision of `CHANGE-BRIEF.md` by me.

## One authority
Exactly one node writes to each animated node. Never add a second writer to one that already has one.
- **The rig's `AnimationPlayer`:** `scripts/raccoon_model.gd` only (`play()` :407, :548; `seek()` :493, :550; `speed_scale`
  :478). `player.gd` writes the model's inputs (`jumping`, `leap`, `squash`, `pitch`), never the player. During `jump`
  and `jump_land` the leap `seek()` (:479-493) must not run. `raccoon_flex.gd`, `raccoon_eat.gd` and the `TwoBoneIK3D`
  write bones after it, as `SkeletonModifier3D`s, by design; they never touch the `AnimationPlayer`.
- **Each balloon's `AnimationPlayer`:** that balloon's own script, its only caller of `play()`. The bite check (game
  code) tells the balloon to pop; it doesn't touch the player itself.
- **The moths' `AnimationPlayer`:** their driver script; it reads `burning()`, writes nothing in the game.
- **Not this change's, already two writers:** the dancers' `AnimationPlayer`s are played by `scripts/camp_person.gd`
  (`_play()` :1008) and sought and sped by `scripts/campsite.gd` (:354-355, :617-623) for the beat. Leave as is; don't copy.

## Godot 4 names
Godot 4 only. Never Godot 3's: `Animation.loop` (a bool), `playback_speed`, `playback_process_mode`, `AnimatedSprite`,
`Spatial`, `Particles`, `SpatialMaterial`, `flags_unshaded`, `params_billboard_mode`, `flags_transparent`.
- **Seen working in this repo:** `AnimationPlayer` `play(name, blend)`, `seek(t, true)`, `speed_scale`,

## Project context

- **Engine:** Godot 4.7.2 stable, GDScript; `config/features` is `"4.7"`, `"Forward Plus"` (`project.godot`); the
  wrapper looks for `Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe` (`scripts/run-test.sh:18`). The project is the repo root, so
  the course's `godot/shaders/`, `godot/animations/`, `godot/tests/` are `shaders/`, `animations/`, `tests/` here.
  Renderer Forward+, 1280 × 720, physics interpolation on (`project.godot`). No `animations/` folder exists yet.
- **Scene:** `res://main.tscn` (`run/main_scene`), one `Node3D` running `scripts/main.gd`, which adds `Campsite.new()`.

### The jump: imported 3D rig (`CHANGE-BRIEF.md`, "The two clips")
- **Rig:** `assets/characters/raccoon_v2.glb` (from `raccoon_v2.blend` by `assets/characters/export_raccoon_v2.py`; its
  actions keyed in `design/character/raccoon_v2/anim.py`). Import: `animation/fps=24`, `_subresources={}`
  (`raccoon_v2.glb.import:34,42`). Loaded by `_build_rigged()` (`scripts/raccoon_model.gd:375`); the model's scene is
  `raccoon_model.tscn`. The `AnimationPlayer` is found in the instanced rig (`raccoon_model.gd:384`) and held in `_anim`.
- **New clips** `jump` and `jump_land` go in the `.glb` as Blender actions (keyed in `anim.py`); loop modes go in the
  `.import`'s `_subresources`, replacing the runtime loop at `raccoon_model.gd:385-386`.
- **State machine:** the state lives in `scripts/player.gd` (`jump()` :431, `_jump_pose()` :440, `_end_jump()` :465,
  `jumping` :159, `signal landed` :13, the `JUMP_*`, `AIR_CONTROL`, `LAND_TIME` constants :93-100; `_physics_process()`
  :251 sets `model.jumping`). The clips are picked in `scripts/raccoon_model.gd`: `_process_rigged()` :460 →
  `_rigged_state()` :553 → `_change_animation()` :540. No `AnimationTree`.
- **His mouth:** `mouth`, a `Marker3D` on the `head` bone (`raccoon_model.gd:392-400`). **Readers of the jump:**
  `cone_driver.gd:96`; `_on_landed()` (`campsite.gd:539`, `HEAR_STEPS` 6 m); `tasks_test.gd:260-274`.

### The balloon's float: `Sprite3D` + `AnimationPlayer` frame track
- **Sheets:** `assets/sprites/balloons/balloon_{red_4,yellow,blue_4}.png` (also green, purple), 48 × 64 px, `hframes` 3,
  `vframes` 2; float cells 0–2, pop 3–5 (`assets/sprites/balloons/ATTRIBUTION.md`; CC-BY-SA 4.0, credit line there).
- **Placement:** by the party's table and speaker, `TABLE` and `SPEAKER` (`scripts/campsite.gd:81,83`); the pop is heard
  `HEAR_CHITTER` 8 m (:105). The balloon's scene, script and clips don't exist yet; their paths are not chosen.
- **Moth (extra):** `assets/sprites/cutebugs/bugs.png` (`ATTRIBUTION.md` there, CC0), shown while `burning()`
  (`scripts/camp_fire.gd`). Both sheets have `detect_3d/compress_to=1` today (their `.png.import`, line 40).

### Tests: always `bash scripts/run-test.sh <test> <fps|realtime> [timeout-s]`, from the repo root
- `--name` runs `main.tscn` with that flag (parsed in `scripts/main.gd:399-470`); anything else runs `res://tests/<file>`
  with `--script`. Headless. `<fps>` adds `--fixed-fps <fps>`; `realtime` omits it (audio, the clock). Timeout 120 s by
  default. Log `logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log` or `_realtime.log`. Exit 1 on `SHADER ERROR`, `SCRIPT ERROR` or `Failed
  loading resource`; 124 on timeout (`scripts/run-test.sh`). Godot from `GODOT`, the PATH, `../Godot/`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%`.
```
bash scripts/run-test.sh a3_asset_check.gd 60          # tests/a3_asset_check.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh normal_map_calibration.gd 60  # tests/normal_map_calibration.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh test_materials.gd 60          # tests/test_materials.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh test_leaf_burst_config.gd 60  # tests/test_leaf_burst_config.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh test_campfire_smoke_config.gd 60  # tests/test_campfire_smoke_config.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh cost_effects.gd 60 300        # tests/cost_effects.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --sound-test 60               # scripts/sound_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --bubble-test 60              # scripts/bubble_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --camp-test 60                # scripts/camp_test.gd (reads campers' current_animation)
bash scripts/run-test.sh --tasks-test 60               # scripts/tasks_test.gd (a jump's landing heard)
bash scripts/run-test.sh --plan-test 60                # scripts/plan_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --tutorial-test 60            # scripts/tutorial_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --cones-test 30               # scripts/cones_test.gd; also 60 and 144
bash scripts/run-test.sh --cone-shader-test 30         # tests/cone_shader_test.gd; also 60 and 144
bash scripts/run-test.sh --fire-test 60                # scripts/fire_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --tent-test 60 300            # scripts/tent_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --bearbag-test 60 300         # scripts/bear_bag_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --leaf-burst-test 60          # tests/leaf_burst_state_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --smoke-test 60               # tests/campfire_smoke_state_test.gd; also --smoke-load-test
bash scripts/run-test.sh --waves-test realtime         # scripts/waves_test.gd; under --fixed-fps one check fails
bash scripts/run-test.sh --title-test realtime         # scripts/title_test.gd; under --fixed-fps one check fails
```
- The waves and title failures under `--fixed-fps` are expected: don't "fix" them. No Assignment 7 test exists yet.

  particle process. Node state (emitting, one_shot, amount_ratio, visibility, instance counts) is observable; the
  look is not. On 4.7.2 a one-shot `GPUParticles3D` turns `emitting` off within a few frames and never emits
  `finished` (read back on 7 Nov 2026), so nothing may wait on `finished`: free a burst on a timer.

- Frame strips come from a windowed Movie Maker run, which I start.
- Under `--fixed-fps`, game time follows frames, not the clock; physics runs at 60 ticks a second at every rate.

bash scripts/run-test.sh --tent-test 60 300            # scripts/tent_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --bearbag-test 60 300         # scripts/bear_bag_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --leaf-burst-test 60          # tests/leaf_burst_state_test.gd
bash scripts/run-test.sh --smoke-test 60               # tests/campfire_smoke_state_test.gd; also --smoke-load-test
bash scripts/run-test.sh --waves-test realtime         # scripts/waves_test.gd; under --fixed-fps one check fails
bash scripts/run-test.sh --title-test realtime         # scripts/title_test.gd; under --fixed-fps one check fails
```
- The waves and title failures under `--fixed-fps` are expected: don't "fix" them. No Assignment 7 test exists yet.
## Headless facts
- A headless run uses a dummy renderer (it reports no video adapter): it draws no particles and runs no GPU
  particle process. Node state (emitting, one_shot, amount_ratio, visibility, instance counts) is observable; the
  look is not. On 4.7.2 a one-shot `GPUParticles3D` turns `emitting` off within a few frames and never emits
  `finished` (read back on 7 Nov 2026), so nothing may wait on `finished`: free a burst on a timer.
- A GPU effect's headless CPU price is near zero by construction.
- Frame strips come from a windowed Movie Maker run, which I start.
- Under `--fixed-fps`, game time follows frames, not the clock; physics runs at 60 ticks a second at every rate.
## Current change
@CHANGE-BRIEF.md

## Ownership
- Every file in `shaders/` is hand-written by the human and is never edited by an agent: not created, rewritten,
  reformatted or "fixed". If a shader looks wrong, report it and stop.
- Clips live as resources: in `animations/` (`.tres`/`.res`), in the scene that owns them (the balloon's `.tscn`), or,
  for the rig, as actions in `raccoon_v2.glb` with import settings in its `.import`. Never built in code at runtime: no
  `Animation.new()`, `add_track()`, `track_insert_key()` or `loop_mode =` in game scripts.
- Assignment 6's effect settings stay in `effects/` scenes. The brief's tables are the source of every timing; a
  change starts as a dated revision of `CHANGE-BRIEF.md`, made by the human.

## One authority
Exactly one node writes to each animated node. Never add a second writer to one that already has one.
- **The rig's `AnimationPlayer`:** `scripts/raccoon_model.gd` only (`play()` :407, :548; `seek()` :493, :550; `speed_scale`
  :478). `player.gd` writes the model's inputs (`jumping`, `leap`, `squash`, `pitch`), never the player. During `jump`
  and `jump_land` the leap `seek()` (:479-493) must not run. `raccoon_flex.gd`, `raccoon_eat.gd` and the `TwoBoneIK3D`
  write bones after it, as `SkeletonModifier3D`s, by design; they never touch the `AnimationPlayer`.
- **Each balloon's `AnimationPlayer`:** that balloon's own script, its only caller of `play()`; the bite check asks it to pop.
- **The moths' `AnimationPlayer`:** their driver script; it reads `burning()`, writes nothing in the game.
- **Not this change's, already two writers:** the dancers' `AnimationPlayer`s are played by `scripts/camp_person.gd`
  (`_play()` :1008) and sought and sped by `scripts/campsite.gd` (:354-355, :617-623) for the beat. Leave as is; don't copy.

## Godot 4 names
Godot 4 only. Never Godot 3's: `Animation.loop` (a bool), `playback_speed`, `playback_process_mode`, `AnimatedSprite`,
`Spatial`, `Particles`, `SpatialMaterial`, `flags_unshaded`, `params_billboard_mode`, `flags_transparent`.
- **Seen working in this repo:** `AnimationPlayer` `play(name, blend)`, `seek(t, true)`, `speed_scale`,
  `current_animation`, `current_animation_position`, `current_animation_length`, `get_animation_list()`,
  `get_animation()`; `Animation.loop_mode`, `Animation.LOOP_LINEAR` (`raccoon_model.gd`). `Sprite3D` `pixel_size`,
  `billboard`, `alpha_cut` (`SpriteBase3D.ALPHA_CUT_*`), `texture_filter` (`BaseMaterial3D.TEXTURE_FILTER_*`) (`main.gd:1264-1275`).
- **Read back on 4.7.2 (the brief):** rig's `callback_mode_process` 1 (`ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_IDLE`), `step` 1/24.
- **Not yet seen in this repo, believed Godot 4; read back from ClassDB before relying on them:** `Animation.LOOP_NONE`,
  `Animation.step`, `length`, `TYPE_VALUE`, `value_track_set_update_mode()`, `UPDATE_DISCRETE`, `track_get_path()`,
  `track_get_key_time()`, `Sprite3D.hframes`/`vframes`/`frame`, `TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST`, `AnimationLibrary`, and the
  glb importer's per-animation `settings/loop_mode` key in `_subresources`.

## Out of scope
- Movement, collision, input and key bindings, except the brief's two jump timings (takeoff 5 ticks after the press,
  a 10-tick landing). No new keys. The leap from the hollow and hops keep the run clip.
- The campers (sight, states, routines, timings, clips), the tutorial, the other tasks, the fire's life; `shaders/`,
  Assignment 6's effects, every other look; the renderer, `project.godot`; the seven raccoon clips' keys (only
  their loop mode moves, into the `.import`).
- What any existing test expects. A test may change how it measures only with the same expected value.
- Presentation reads game state and never writes it; the bite, the pops and the task are game code.

## Unconfirmed
- Whether the glb importer on 4.7.2 keeps `settings/loop_mode` per animation from `_subresources` after an empty-cache
  `--import`: the brief's prediction, not yet read back.
- How a continuous-update `frame` track rounds between keys on 4.7.2 (the brief's short answer 2).
- The pose-vs-game disagreement of one physics tick (1/60 s) is predicted, not measured.
- Paths for the balloon and moth scenes and scripts and the Assignment 7 tests: in no file yet. `--jump-test`
  (`scripts/main.gd:412,766`) only presses jump for a screenshot; it checks nothing.
- Earlier counts were measured 11 Nov 2026 (`logs/a6-run-scribe-cones/`); rerun before trusting. `run-test.sh`'s
  third argument is only the timeout, so `--*-shots=<folder>` options can't go through it.

I've revised CLAUDE.md and it's now 118 lines. No other file was changed, nothing is committed, and I stopped there. Nothing was run: everything in it comes from reading the files, and each fact carries its file and line.

**The sections, in your order:**
- **AGENTS.md:** there isn't one, so there's no `@AGENTS.md` line.
- **Project context:** Godot 4.7.2 with Forward+. The jump is on the rig (`raccoon_v2.glb`, its `.import`, and `_build_rigged()`). The state is in `player.gd`, and the clips are picked by `_process_rigged()` → `_rigged_state()` → `_change_animation()` in `raccoon_model.gd`. The balloons get their sheets, where they'll stand (`TABLE`/`SPEAKER`) and how far a pop is heard (`HEAR_CHITTER`). The moth's sheet is there too, with the scene they all appear in and the full test list through `run-test.sh`, including `realtime`.
- **Headless facts:** kept word for word, in the same place.
- **Current change:** unchanged.
- **Ownership:** the `shaders/` rule is kept. I added that clips live in `animations/`, in the scene that owns them, or as `.glb` actions with their settings in the `.import`, and are never built in code at runtime. I shortened the Assignment 6 `effects/` rule to one line.
- **One authority:** one writer for the rig, one for each balloon and one for the moths, with the line numbers where it writes. It also says the leap `seek()` mustn't run during `jump` or `jump_land`.
- **Godot 4 names:** split into names seen working in this repo, names the brief read back, and names I think exist but haven't seen here. The last group includes `LOOP_NONE`, `step`, `UPDATE_DISCRETE`, `hframes`/`vframes`/`frame`, and the importer's `settings/loop_mode` key. They're flagged to be read back from ClassDB before anyone relies on them.
- **Out of scope** and **Unconfirmed:** follow the brief. Unconfirmed also notes that the Assignment 7 test names and the balloon and moth file paths aren't in any file yet.

**Things you may want to look at before you review:**
- **The dancers' animations already have two writers.** `camp_person.gd` plays them (`_play()`, line 1008), and `campsite.gd` seeks them and sets their speed to keep them on the beat (lines 354–355 and 617–623). That breaks the one-writer rule. I didn't touch it, because the campers are out of scope, and I wrote it into "One authority" as a case not to copy.
- **`--jump-test` doesn't test anything.** It's an existing flag in `main.gd` (lines 412 and 766) that only presses jump for a screenshot. It isn't in the test list, but its name makes it look like a check, so I noted it under Unconfirmed.
- **I dropped the old test counts** from 11 Nov, since the records were reset for Assignment 7. Unconfirmed still says to rerun them before trusting them.
- **The tutorial check's count disagrees between files:** README.md says 29 checks and the old CLAUDE.md said 34. I didn't settle it.
